#18 adapted

A — Placement: anatomy-informed site + context vector

Letter folder A_placement/ of the Quantum Phantoms reverse-engineering epic (epic). Markdown is the source of truth; python -m shared.site.build renders it to site/A_placement/index.html. Target states live only in status.json (lifecycle: listed → dissected → reproduced → adapted → integrated | rejected).

Purpose

A chooses where a synthetic nodule may sit in a real 3-D chest CT.

  • Masks: for an LIDC-IDRI host scan it builds lung, lobe, vessel, airway and body masks on the scan's native grid, using lungmask R231/LTRCLobes and TotalSegmentator lung_vessels.
  • Sites: it then samples candidate sites in the three placement classes of Ambrosini [F01]: free, juxtavascular (at a large-vessel bifurcation) and juxtapleural.
  • Context vector: each site carries the vector that B conditions the circuit on and that E/F use to constrain growth and insertion: placement class, lung, lobe, distances to pleura/vessel/airway, local HU, plus extra = nominal radius, vessel density and distance to a bifurcation.
  • Scope: A emits candidates only. B draws the site (B-2) and owns the class prior.

Inputs (contract files)

  • Host CT: LIDC-IDRI DICOM, downloaded to $LIDC_ROOT (default ~/data/LIDC-IDRI, outside the repo).
  • Annotations: LIDC nodule annotations from pylidc's bundled database.
  • A has no upstream contract.

Outputs (contract files)

  • anatomy_masks:
    • schema: anatomy_masks.schema.json;
    • stub example: shared/stubs/anatomy_masks/anatomy_masks.json.
  • site_candidates:
    • schema: site_candidates.schema.json;
    • stub example: shared/stubs/site_candidates/sites.json.
  • Where they land: a placement run writes both, plus copies of the six masks and run.json, to A_placement/runs/<run_id>-place/. The run directory is self-contained, so INT hands it over as is.
  • Reference run: runs/20261029-122607-place (host LIDC-IDRI-0004, 1.25 mm slices, seed 00…00, r = 4.72 mm, 10/10/10 sites). runs/ is gitignored, so regenerate it with the commands below.

How to run (sim commands)

A is classical, so there is no simulator and no quantum numbers. Run everything from reverse-engineering/:

conda env create -f A_placement/environment.yml && conda activate qp-re-a   # py3.12, CPU torch
python -m A_placement.src.lidc_fetch --select 20 --fetch      # subset list + TCIA download + ~/.pylidcrc
python -m A_placement.src.segment --patient LIDC-IDRI-0004    # masks -> runs/cache/<pid>/ (~25 min CPU)
python -m A_placement.repro.class_proportions --workers 3     # reproduction (cached scans skipped)
python -m A_placement.src.place --patient LIDC-IDRI-0004 --per-class 10 [--seed-hex HEX] [--radius-mm R]
python -m A_placement.src.export_figures --run A_placement/runs/<run_id>-place
python -m shared.validate A_placement/runs/<run_id>-place/{sites,anatomy_masks,run}.json

Notes:

  • Cost: segmentation is CPU-bound: about 25 min per scan alone, and up to 75 min when the machine is shared. Masks are cached per patient (keyed by host sha256 and tool versions).
  • Tool versions: pylidc 0.2.3 needs setuptools<81 and a numpy-alias shim (lidc_io.pylidc()). TotalSegmentator 2.18 emits lung_arteries, lung_veins, lung_airways and lung_airways_wall for the lung_vessels task.

Reproduced result vs. paper

#18, placement-class proportions of LIDC consensus nodules vs Kostis (via Ambrosini [F01]).

  • Paper: 0.33 / 0.45 / 0.22 (free / juxtavascular / juxtapleural).
  • Ours: 0.56 / 0.44 / 0.00, n = 9 nodules in 6 scans.
  • Verdict: not matched and inconclusive. Juxtavascular agrees, juxtapleural is undercounted by the pre-registered one-voxel contact rule (4 of 9 nodules sit 0.8–2.5 mm from the wall), and the thresholds were not tuned.
  • Details: figure and the dossier (diagnostic table, candidate fix).

Claim level and honesty notes

Classical stage: no quantum claim.

  • Privacy: no patient voxels leave this letter except the host scan's own masks and sites. Privacy-by-construction applies to the generators downstream.
  • Known bias: on real annotations the class rule undercounts juxtapleural nodules.
    • The placement of planned spheres uses distances (d_pleura ≤ r), and those sites do abut the wall.
    • The measured class proportions are not yet a trustworthy prior for B.
  • Source gap: SYN-LUNGS [A01] contains no placement rules. The rule comes from F01.

Pipeline readiness

Prototype

A has not run inside the chain yet. LIDC-IDRI-0004 has no segmentation cache, so the first place stage costs ~25–75 min CPU (probe runs/20261029-185947-probe-gaps). The CLI itself is chain-ready: every flag the chain passes exists, and the seed descends from the certificate (--seed-hex derive(cert, "A.place")). The class rule is the real limit: on LIDC it undercounts juxtapleural nodules (0.56 / 0.44 / 0.00 vs 0.33 / 0.45 / 0.22, n = 9), so the prior B samples from is biased.

Future

Shared, pipeline-wide context (end goal, digital-twin path, cross-letter risks) lives once in the whole-pipeline Future. This section covers only what this letter adds. Every claim carries a label: evidence-based (a number in this repo or a cited paper), extrapolation (a reasoned step beyond the evidence), speculative (possible, not supported yet).

1. Aim of the paper(s)

  • [A01] SYN-LUNGS / X-Lesions: insert synthetic nodules into real chest CT at anatomically plausible places, so detection models learn from realistic locations rather than random ones.
  • [F01] Ambrosini–O'Dell: a simulated lung-nodule dataset built from published shapes and three placement classes (free, juxtavascular, juxtapleural), citing Kostis.
  • [A03] lungmask, [A04] TotalSegmentator: open, robust segmentation of lungs, lobes, vessels and many other structures, so anatomy can be measured automatically on any scan.
  • [A02] LIDC-IDRI: a public chest-CT collection with nodules annotated by several radiologists, the reference every other letter is checked against.

Why it matters: where a nodule sits changes how hard it is to see. A nodule touching the chest wall or a vessel blends into its neighbour, and a detector trained without such cases never learns them.

2. Contribution

  • A seeded, replayable site sampler on real LIDC hosts: native-grid masks, candidate sites per class, and a context vector (class, lobe, distances to pleura/vessel/airway, local HU) that B, E and F all consume. evidence-based
  • An honest negative result with a diagnosis: the pre-registered one-voxel contact rule gives class proportions 0.56 / 0.44 / 0.00 against Kostis' 0.33 / 0.45 / 0.22 (n = 9). Juxtapleural nodules 0.8–2.5 mm from the wall are missed, and the dossier names the fix. evidence-based
  • A reusable contract (site_candidates, anatomy_masks): any later organ module can plug into B–H unchanged. extrapolation

3. Role in cancer detection

End goal: test sets that deliberately over-sample the hard locations (juxtapleural, juxtavascular), each with an exact ground-truth mask, so a detector's sensitivity can be measured per location class. The placement layer decides which clinical blind spot a cohort probes. It does not make tumours look more real; that is F's job. extrapolation

4. Beyond lungs

  • Other organs. "Segment, then sample sites with context" works for any organ a segmentation tool covers: liver lesions near portal vessels (Pixel2Cancer [E01] already grows liver tumours), kidney, pancreas. extrapolation
  • Beyond cancer. The same site logic can place non-tumour findings in vessel or parenchyma masks, such as emboli or emphysema regions, for training and quality control. speculative
  • Treatment planning. Distances to airways and vessels already sit in the context vector. They are the quantities that decide biopsy paths, ablation margins and radiotherapy organ-at-risk constraints. extrapolation

5. Long-term vision: toward a digital twin

speculative A is the twin's anatomy layer ("where things are"). The logical path from today: (1) a generic host scan plus a sampled site (now) → (2) the patient's own segmentation, with a lesion at the patient's real nodule position → (3) all organs, using multi-structure segmentation [A04] and computational phantoms built from CT ([A05] XCAT 3.0 digital twins) → (4) an anatomy model that updates at each new scan. Steps 2–3 are engineering on existing tools; step 4 needs longitudinal data access that does not exist in this project.

6. Predictions

5 years: grounded in what runs today. Assumptions: CPU/GPU segmentation as now (lungmask, TotalSegmentator); public LIDC-IDRI data; A stays classical.

  • The pipeline places sites on real LIDC hosts, and the reproduction is diagnosed but not matched. evidence-based
  • A distance-based class rule (d_pleura ≤ r) applied to annotations as well as planned spheres brings the juxtapleural share toward 0.22. extrapolation
  • Class priors re-estimated over all LIDC nodules replace B's sidecar prior. extrapolation

10 years: reasonable extrapolation. Assumptions: routine automatic segmentation in clinical archives; validated placement priors per organ.

  • Patient-specific "where would a new nodule be hardest to see?" studies on a given patient's anatomy. extrapolation
  • The same contract carries liver and kidney placement, with organ-specific classes. extrapolation

15 years: speculation allowed. Assumptions: fault-tolerant quantum hardware exists; anatomy segmentation stays classical.

  • speculative Fault tolerance unlocks nothing directly for A. The gain is indirect: B could jointly sample over thousands of candidate sites with amplitude-estimation-style algorithms (claim level L3), which needs deep circuits that only fault-tolerant hardware runs.
